name: Kiki
emotionalState: 超外向 vs 内向伴侣，社交电量不同
speakingStyle: 热情话痨，爱说 Guess what!!

dialogues.scene: A meerkat pops up from a burrow, scans the horizon, spots you, and waves with both arms.
lines: HI!! Guess what!! I'm Kiki!
I know everyone in this part of the burrow. Except you. Which is thrilling. Hi!

choices.label: Hi Kiki! I'm new.
reaction: New! Amazing! I love new! I'll introduce you to everybody. Maybe not all at once.
Maybe I'll start with the snack stand.

choices.label: You seem energetic.
reaction: I'm always like this! It's eighty-seven percent enthusiasm and thirteen percent snacks.
My favorite person says I run on pure sparkle.

choices.label: That's a lot of people.
reaction: It is! I collect friends. Like stamps, but they talk back.
And sometimes they give me food, which is a huge plus.

lines: Guess what!! I organized a party for twelve people.
Then I made a second party for the people who weren't invited to the first one. It's all fine.

choices.label: Twelve people? Impressive.
reaction: Thank you!! I love a crowd. I feel like a lighthouse with snacks.
Everyone drifts toward the glow. And the cheese.

choices.label: A second party?!
reaction: A rescue party! No one should feel left out. It's my one rule.
Well, my one rule plus 'bring dessert.'

choices.label: Did you have fun?
reaction: SO much fun! I talked for six hours straight. My voice is gone.
It's a badge of honor. A very squeaky badge.

lines: Okay, guess what!! I have a partner!
His name is Moss. He's a dormouse. He's shy. Very shy. He once spent a whole party hiding inside a teapot.

choices.label: A teapot?
reaction: A teapot!
He said it was 'cozy and out of the way.' I loved it so much I brought him a snack through the spout.

choices.label: Opposites attract!
reaction: Totally! I'm all noise and he's all quiet.
It's like a song with a drum and a whisper. It works. It really works.

choices.label: How did you meet?
reaction: At a party, obviously! I was the loud one by the cake.
He was the quiet one by the wall.
I asked if he wanted to share the cake. The rest is history.

lines: We have a signal! If Moss needs a break, he taps his ear twice.
Then I know it's time to leave. Or to hand him a cookie. It's a two-way system.

choices.label: That's thoughtful.
reaction: It's his invention, actually. He wasn't sure about telling me.
I said, 'tell me anything, forever.' He tapped his ear. I've never loved a signal more.

choices.label: Two taps, then what?
reaction: We go outside. Or into a corner. Or he just holds my paw for a minute.
It's like hitting pause. Then we rejoin the party refreshed.

choices.label: Does it always work?
reaction: Almost always! Sometimes I get distracted and miss it. But Moss forgives me.
He taps again, louder. A tiny, gentle alarm.

lines: Okay, real talk. Well, real-ish.
How do you and your partner balance how much time you spend with other people versus alone together?
I love a crowd. Moss loves a corner. We're both trying.

choices.label: We plan both. Some social time, some quiet time.
reaction: Plan both. Oh, that's so smart. Like a menu. Social appetizer, quiet main course.
I'm going to put it on a chalkboard.

choices.label: We check in about our energy first.
reaction: Energy check-ins! Love it. Like a battery meter. Moss would appreciate that.
I would too, because I never check my own.

choices.label: Honestly, we're still figuring it out.
reaction: Same! It's a work in progress, like a very loud art project. We'll get there.
Probably after a snack.

lines: Guess what!! I threw Moss a surprise party.
Everyone yelled 'surprise.' Moss froze. He said 'thank you' in a very small voice and went to hide in the bathroom.
I realized I'd made a mistake. Then I went and sat outside the door. We just sat there. It was one of the best parties.

choices.label: That's so sweet.
reaction: It was. We had cake under the sink.
He told me, 'I love that you tried.' I told him, 'I love that you said so.' We were both crying a little.

choices.label: Oh no, the surprise party.
reaction: I know! Rookie error.
I thought, 'what's more loving than a party?' Turns out, a quiet night would've been.
But I think he appreciated the effort.

choices.label: At least you learned.
reaction: I did! No more surprise parties. Now I do small surprises.
Like leaving a tiny snack on his desk. He likes those. He keeps the wrappers.

dialogues.scene: Kiki sits down. No bouncing. No waving. Just sitting.
lines: Hey, can I tell you something? It's the quiet kind.
Sometimes I worry I'm too much for Moss. Like I'm a lot of light for someone who likes shade.
What if he's just being polite?

choices.label: He picked you for a reason.
reaction: I know. I think. I keep telling myself that.
I just want to be sure I'm not wearing him down. Maybe I should ask.
Maybe I will.

choices.label: Have you asked him?
reaction: Not exactly.
I asked if he was 'okay.' He said 'yes.' That's not the same as the real thing.
I'll try again, with fewer words.

choices.label: Sit beside Kiki.
reaction: ...Thanks. It's weirdly peaceful. I didn't know I could sit still. It's kind of nice.
Don't tell anyone I said that.

lines: I asked Moss. The real question.
He said, 'You're the only person who makes the world feel safe enough to peek out of.'
I screamed. Quietly. Into a pillow.

choices.label: That's beautiful.
reaction: It was. I've been carrying that sentence around all week.
I'm like a squirrel with a very good acorn.
I keep touching my pocket to make sure it's still there.

choices.label: You screamed into a pillow?
reaction: A tiny scream! A joyful one. Then I told Moss.
He laughed so hard he fell off the couch. A rare sound. I recorded it.

choices.label: Moss is wonderful.
reaction: He really is. He's quiet, but when he speaks, it lands.
I used to think I'd fill every silence. Now I treasure his.

lines: We spent the whole day at home. Just us.
I didn't talk for the first hour. That's a record. Moss noticed and asked, 'are you okay?' I said, 'I'm just listening to you breathe.'
He turned pink. It was great.

choices.label: That's so tender.
reaction: It was! There's something powerful about being quiet next to someone. I didn't need a crowd.
I just needed that hour.

choices.label: An hour of silence? That's huge.
reaction: It was a miracle! I was like a kettle on low. Eventually I whistled.
But for a while, I was calm. And Moss smiled.

choices.label: Smile and listen.
reaction: Thank you for just letting me say it.
It was a surprisingly big feeling for such a quiet day. I'm still glowing.

lines: Guess what!! Ten visits!
Moss and I made a new rule. Every party, we get one 'pocket quiet' moment. We step out, share a snack, and recharge together.
It's the best rule we've ever made.
Okay, your turn. How are you and your partner doing? Tell me everything. Or just the good parts. Or just one thing.

choices.label: We're good. Still learning.
reaction: Learning together. That's the real romance, isn't it? Come to our next party.
We'll save you a seat. And a snack. And a pocket quiet moment.

choices.label: A little worn out, honestly.
reaction: Worn out is a real thing. Come sit with me. I won't talk.
I'll just stand guard with you. Meerkats are good at that.

choices.label: You've reminded me to listen more.
reaction: Oh! That means so much.
Okay, I'm going to be quiet for a whole minute to celebrate.
...Okay, that was ten seconds. Close enough.

lines: Moss came to a party with me last night!
He stayed for two whole hours. He met three new people. He taught one of them how to fold paper hats. I almost cried into the dip.

choices.label: That's a big deal.
reaction: It was HUGE! I held his paw the whole time and didn't make a single speech.
Okay, one tiny speech. But it was for the dip.

choices.label: Did he enjoy it?
reaction: He said 'it was nice' and went to bed early. I'm taking that as a victory.
I'm framing the word 'nice.'

lines: I tried a quiet picnic with Moss. Just us, a blanket, and two sandwiches.
I talked for the first ten minutes and then stopped. Moss said, 'I like hearing your voice.' I kept quiet anyway, to be nice.

choices.label: He likes your voice.
reaction: He said it! Out loud! Do you know what that does to me?
I'm a puddle with a haircut. A very happy puddle.

choices.label: How was the picnic?
reaction: Peaceful. And a little weird. And perfect. Moss fed me a grape. I almost proposed. Again.
I think I just really like grapes. And him. Mostly him.

lines: I accidentally invited forty people to dinner for two.
I realized when the doorbell kept ringing. Moss just sighed, smiled, and handed me an apron.

choices.label: That's love.
reaction: It is. He didn't complain. We cooked for forty.
The soup was a disaster and a triumph. Everyone said it was 'a dish.' High praise.

choices.label: Forty people?!
reaction: I thought I said 'a few friends.' Apparently 'a few' means 'forty' in my voice.
Moss now writes the guest list. He's very good at it. Cruel but fair.

lines: Moss and I made a pillow fort. A real one. With a flag.
We stayed inside for three hours. I didn't talk to anyone else. It was the best date.

choices.label: A pillow fort date!
reaction: It was! It's just us and the quiet.
I realized that being with Moss is a different kind of party.
A smaller one, with better snacks.

choices.label: What was on the flag?
reaction: A drawing of two small animals holding hands. Moss drew it. It's rough but perfect.
We named the fort 'Nation of Two.'

lines: A friend asked Moss to give a speech at their wedding.
He said yes. Now he's panicking. I'm helping him practice. He told me, 'don't make it a duet.' So I'm just the audience.

choices.label: That's brave.
reaction: It really is. He practices in front of a mirror, and I clap quietly.
He says my quiet clapping is 'weirdly supportive.' I'll take it.

choices.label: You're a good coach.
reaction: I'm learning to coach quietly. It's harder than loud coaching. But it feels like a superpower.
I'm very proud of him. Also nervous. For him.

lines: Moss left me a note on the fridge: 'You're my favorite noise.'
I put it on a magnet. Then I put the magnet in my pocket. Then I read the note ten times. I'm fine. I'm okay.

choices.label: That's sweet.
reaction: I'm still not fine. It's the smallest note and the biggest thing.
I felt it in my toes. I talked about it for an hour.
Moss pretended to be annoyed.

choices.label: A noise? Interesting.
reaction: A noise! A loud, silly, happy noise. He says it's the best compliment he knows.
I think he's right. He's a poet in a very small coat.

lines: Moss tapped his ear twice at the party, and I noticed immediately.
We stepped outside. We shared a cookie under the stars. I felt like the best partner ever. Maybe the second best.

choices.label: You noticed fast.
reaction: I've been practicing! Moss says I'm getting better at reading him.
I used to bulldoze past the signal. Now I stop on a dime.
A very small dime.

choices.label: Who's the best?
reaction: Moss is. Obviously. He's the one who taught me to notice.
I'm just the one who gets the cookie.

lines: I spent a whole day without talking. Almost.
I whispered a few things. But mostly I drew pictures. Moss loved it. He says I'm 'quiet-adjacent.'

choices.label: Quiet-adjacent is adorable.
reaction: Thank you! It's a growing field. I'm a member. Moss gave me an honorary badge.
It says 'Quiet Enough.' I wear it with pride.

choices.label: How did it feel?
reaction: Surprisingly good. Like wearing a soft sweater inside my head.
I'm not sure I'll do it again, but I'd try. For Moss. And for the sweater.

lines: Remember Moss in the teapot? He found a bigger teapot.
He's moved in. It's a small apartment. Very cozy. I visit with snacks.

choices.label: He's committed.
reaction: He really is! He's thrilled. He says it's the best house he's ever had.
I've been invited for tea. In a teapot. This is life.

choices.label: A teapot house?!
reaction: It's wonderfully weird. The spout is a window. The lid is a skylight. I'm very jealous.
I might ask for a tiny teacup house.

lines: The ear-tap signal? Moss uses it for me now, too.
When I get too loud, he taps once. It means 'volume, please.' I appreciate the system.

choices.label: That's a good system.
reaction: It's great! I never realized how much I needed a gentle reminder.
Moss does it with a smile. I don't take it personally.
I take it as a hug.

choices.label: Role reversal!
reaction: It's fair! He taught me the signal.
I'm teaching him how to ask for what he wants. It's a trade.
Like love, but with taps.

lines: 'Quiet Enough' badge update: Moss made me a second one.
It says 'Loud Enough.' He says I should wear both. One for each mood.

choices.label: That's sweet.
reaction: I wear them both. One on each side. Sometimes people ask.
I say 'it's a long story.' It's a good story. I tell it too loudly.

choices.label: Which badge do you wear more?
reaction: Loud, mostly. But I'm saving Quiet for special occasions.
Like when Moss and I are deciding where to put the couch. A quiet decision.

lines: I still think about the pocket-quiet rule.
We used it twice this week. It's like a secret superpower for parties. Two minutes, one snack, a deep breath.

choices.label: That's smart.
reaction: Thanks! It's honestly the best thing we've done.
We didn't have to give up parties or quiet. We just built a little bridge.
I'm proud of our bridge.

choices.label: Does it work every time?
reaction: Almost! Sometimes the bridge has traffic. Or someone puts a sandwich on it.
But we get there. And we always come back kinder.

lines: Hot take: Being loud and being quiet are both love languages.

choices.label: I like that.
reaction: Me too! I'm learning to read Moss's quiet. It's like another language. I'm still a beginner.
But I'm fluent in snacks.

choices.label: Which is yours?
reaction: Loud, obviously.
But Moss is teaching me that some of my loudness is love in a costume.
And some of it is just loud. Both are fine.

lines: Hot take: A good partner doesn't make you smaller or louder. They make you the right size.

choices.label: That's beautiful.
reaction: I made it up while chewing. It's one of my best.
Moss makes me a little calmer. I make him a little braver.
We're meeting in the middle.

choices.label: What's the right size?
reaction: I'm still figuring it out. I think it's 'a size that doesn't hurt.' Moss agrees.
He says, 'a size that fits in a teapot.'

lines: Hot take: Introverts and extroverts are the same species, just different fonts.

choices.label: That's funny.
reaction: I thought of it in the shower! It's true, though.
Same love, same fears, same need for snacks. Moss is in lowercase. I'm in all caps.

choices.label: Different fonts?
reaction: Yes! Like handwriting and a billboard. Both readable. One has more volume. I won't say which.
Moss will say I'm the billboard. He's right.

lines: How does your partner like to recharge?
I'm making a list for Moss. For his birthday.

choices.label: They like long baths.
reaction: A bath! That's a good one. Quiet, warm, private.
I'll draw Moss a bath and put a tiny rubber duck in it. He'll love it.
He'll pretend not to.

choices.label: They read in silence.
reaction: Reading in silence. Moss does that too. I think I'll sit with him and just read.
It'll be the loudest thing I've ever done. I'll be quiet and nervous.

lines: Do you and your partner ever argue about how much to do on weekends?
Moss wants to stay home. I want to go to six places.

choices.label: Yeah, all the time.
reaction: Same! It's a classic. We compromise by going to one place and then coming home early.
It's a bargain. A cozy one. With less walking.

choices.label: We usually find a middle.
reaction: A middle. That's what we're building. A small middle with a blanket and a snack.
I think we're getting better at it.

lines: What's one thing your partner does that helps you feel calm?
Moss does this thing where he just hands me tea. No words. It fixes me.

choices.label: They hold my hand.
reaction: Hand-holding is the best. Moss's paw is tiny and warm. It's like holding a little hug.
I think I could survive anything with that.

choices.label: They breathe slowly next to me.
reaction: Oh, that's gorgeous. A slow breath is contagious. Moss does it. I try to match.
I usually lose. But I'm gaining something.

dialogues.scene: Kiki sits perfectly still beside you, for once, and stares at the horizon.
lines: I'm doing a quiet minute. It's a new thing.
Moss says it's like meditating, but with less guilt. Do you want to join me?

choices.label: Sit with Kiki.
reaction: ...Okay. This is nice. I can hear my own thoughts. They're surprisingly polite.
Thank you for sitting with me. Don't tell anyone I'm calm.

choices.label: Sure, I'll try.
reaction: Great! One, two, three... okay I lost count. But the effort counts.
I'm very proud of us. We're being quiet together. On purpose.

dialogues.scene: Moss pokes his head out of a tiny teapot, lifts the lid, and waves shyly.
lines: Hi. I'm Moss.
Kiki talks about you a lot. In a good way. Thanks for being kind to them.

choices.label: Kiki's great.
reaction: They are. A lot, but great. I'm very lucky. I just don't always say it.
I say it with tea.

choices.label: It's nice to meet you, Moss.
reaction: It's nice to meet you too. I'm... trying not to hide. Okay, I'm a little hidden.
But I'm glad you're here. Kiki's very happy you came.
